items.headline: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
items.excerpt: Jensen Huang’s leather jacket, traders busting out fax machines during the Outlook outage, mega paydays for AI talent, and first-class Frontier tickets for $129: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: AI Tools Huang Championed Now Star in Memes of His Downfall
items.excerpt: Once artificial intelligence’s leading hype-man, Jensen Huang is now the face of an AI-driven meme craze.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO Tests Investor Appetite for AI
items.excerpt: Bloomberg Technology co-host Ed Ludlow tells Bloomberg This Weekend why Anthropic’s upcoming IPO could be a major test of investor appetite for AI, with the offering heavily oversubscribed and poised to follow SpaceX’s blockbuster debut. items.headline: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Access to Users’ Photos
items.excerpt: The Italian Data Protection Authority fined Meta Platforms Inc. €805 million ($887 million) for accessing photos and videos of Android users’ galleries without their explicit consent.

items.headline: Nvidia Looks for a New Era After Huang
items.excerpt: Bloomberg’s Emily Chang tells Bloomberg This Weekend what her recent interview with Jensen Huang reveals about Nvidia’s succession challenge after the longtime CEO’s abrupt departure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Chang examines who could succeed Huang, the questions

items.headline: Couples Are Bringing AI Into Their Arguments
items.excerpt: Bloomberg Weekend senior writer Morgan Meaker tells Bloomberg This Weekend how people are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for advice, validation and even mediation during arguments with their partners. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Meaker explores when AI can improve

items.headline: “Bigger Than a Business Story”: Nvidia Shakeup
items.excerpt: At the end of a week that saw revelations of ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affairs with employees and a suspected Chinese spy, Centerview Partners Senior Counselor Richard Haass says the national security implications go beyond the consequences for the company itself. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Tech Giants Face More Grid Cost Pressure on Democratic Sweep
items.excerpt: Tech giants chasing the infinite promise of AI are finding themselves increasingly on the hook for something far earthier — the electrical grid. A Democratic sweep will only intensify that.

items.headline: Nvidia’s Leadership Shakeup Tests AI Chip Giant
items.excerpt: Bloomberg senior technology and strategic industries editor Mike Shepard tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Nvidia’s appointment of longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO may offer investors some stability after Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina

items.headline: Microsoft Says Services Fully Restored After Outage Roiled World
items.excerpt: Microsoft Corp. said access has been fully restored to its flagship software, ending an outage that paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses around the world.

items.headline: White House Urges Easing Liability to Encourage AI Disclosure
items.excerpt: At a White House meeting on Thursday, officials from President Donald Trump’s artificial intelligence task force recommended that agencies ease their cyber liability policies in an effort to incentivize AI companies to report critical incidents.

items.headline: SpaceX Starship Launches on Flight Test of Reusability
items.excerpt: SpaceX’s Starship rocket took off from the Starbase launch facility in South Texas on a flight test to bring both sections of the vehicle safely back to Earth. Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Colette Kress Will Face Scrutiny at Nvidia
items.excerpt: Nina Trentmann, senior editor at Bloomberg News, says Colette Kress is likely to become more visible as Nvidia’s interim CEO, speaking more about the company’s finances, performance and plans after Jensen Huang’s departure. She speaks with Vonnie Quinn on “The Close”. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Modine Shares Gain Most in Six Years After Samsung Buyout Talks
items.excerpt: Modine Manufacturing Co. logged its biggest single-day gain since 2020 after Bloomberg News reported the maker of cooling systems for data centers was in talks to be acquired by Samsung Electronics Co.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley’s Shalett ‘Incredibly’ Bullish Despite AI Turmoil
items.excerpt: Nvidia Corp.’s leadership turmoil and the Democrats’ midterm election victories have added to concerns about the artificial intelligence boom, but those won’t derail the main driver of the bull market: capital spending on AI infrastructure, says Morgan Stanley Wealth Management’s Lisa Shalett.

items.headline: Match Group Keeping AI Out of Dating
items.excerpt: Match Group is embracing artificial intelligence across its business, but CEO Spencer Rascoff says AI agents won't be allowed to date for users on Tinder, Hinge and its other apps. items.excerpt: Hundreds of Amazon.com Inc. warehouse employees in western Canada are the company’s first North American logistics workers to be covered by a union contract after an independent arbitrator on Friday imposed terms between the online retailer and Unifor, one of the largest private-sector unions in

items.headline: FBI Said to Probe Whether Software Update Caused Mass FAA Outage
items.excerpt: The Federal Bureau of Investigation doesn’t believe the communication issue affecting air traffic control was due to a cyberattack or criminality, said a person familiar with the matter. One area of inquiry is whether the outage was caused by a software update, the person said.

items.headline: Nvidia Crisis Spurs Scrutiny of Agency That Oversees Chip Curbs
items.excerpt: The Trump administration official who runs US export control programs was looking for marquee names for his agency’s upcoming annual conference and threw an unusual option into the mix: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.

items.headline: Blackstone’s QTS Is Cutting AI Debt Sale by More Than Half
items.excerpt: QTS, a data center operator backed by Blackstone Inc., is slashing the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60% after struggling to attract enough demand from investors — and refusing to pay much higher yields.
